claim: The NP-hardness of deciding whether the Kleene star of a star-free regular expression is not co-finite is preserved when the alphabet is restricted to binary and/or when the language of the expression consists of words of only two different lengths.
falsifier: One can construct a reduction from 3SAT to a star-free regular expression over a binary alphabet or with two word lengths such that the co-finiteness condition is equivalent to satisfiability, and verify that the reduction is polynomial.

conditions: E is a star-free regular expression
The alphabet is binary, or the language of E contains words of only two distinct lengths, or both
The decision is whether E* is not co-finite
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the formal setting and proof conditions reported in the source; transfer beyond this setting is unestablished.

title: Decision problem: given–decision problem remains NP-hard theorem
